A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HOT3D and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched despite the relocation of references and appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original hand-tracking, object-pose, segmentation, and 3D-lifting experiments in Tables 2–5, with additional split-specific results in Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and the split-specific results in appendix Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The multi-view FoundPose extension and HandProxy, MonoDepth, and StereoMatch procedures are retained. Revised template-score wording and the clarification that MonoDepth aggregates 3D points do not establish an altered algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same HOT3D, UmeTrack, EgoHOS, and proprietary Aria data coverage and the same evaluated tasks. Changes to the related-dataset table do not change training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–7 retain the same comparisons: UmeTrack and FoundPose view variants, EgoHOS/MRCNN/MRCNN-DA, and HandProxy/MonoDepth/StereoMatch. HO-Cap appears in related-work comparisons, not as a newly evaluated method.

E3.justification: V2 revises the stated prediction coordinate frame from camera space in v1 Section 4.4 to headset space in Section 4. Section 3 also changes the reported Aria recording count from 199 to 198, inconsistently with Appendix A.3. Splits, metrics, and frame sampling remain unchanged; these reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The cross-dataset hand-tracking comparisons, view comparisons, RGB/depth segmentation variants, ground-truth versus predicted-mask evaluations, and qualitative experimental examples are retained. Appendix D's object-orientation analysis is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the reported experiments. Statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All experimental scores in Tables 2–7 are unchanged. V2 adds the breakdown of 1983 Aria and 1849 Quest 3 clips, changes the reported Aria recording count from 199 to 198, and changes HO-3D's objects-per-scene entry in Table 1 from approximately 6 to 1.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical definitions or derivations. Existing geometric descriptions and evaluation criteria are retained.

C1.justification: V1's introduction says the results demonstrate advantages of both multi-view and temporal data; v2 limits this experimental emphasis to multi-view data. The central dataset, baseline-method, and multi-view superiority contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly attributes MonoDepth's optical-axis localization error explicitly to inaccurate depth predictions. Section 4.3 removes the specific camera-configuration explanation from the EgoHOS domain-gap discussion while retaining the broader domain-gap interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 documents clip visibility and overexposure checks, clarifies the canonical-pose hand-skeleton input, and explains MonoDepth's 3D-point aggregation. It removes the explicit baseline-code release commitment and the statement that onboarding sequences lack ground-truth hand poses; actual resource availability changes are not established.

R1.justification: ENIGMA-51 is removed from the 3D-annotation comparison table and cited among datasets providing 2D annotations. A new paragraph positions HO-Cap against HOT3D's capture and annotation approach. HOCAP and HO-Cap refer to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits and locally rewrites the abstract, introduction, and experimental explanations, introduces the HOT3D-Clips name, expands acknowledgements, and adds an appendix overview. References move before the appendices, while the scientific section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 removes the ENIGMA-51 row and reorders HO-Cap, and Figure 2 replaces one sample image. Figure 9 changes columns, and appendix figures and tables are reflowed, with Tables 6–7 placed together on the final page.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity through explicit hand-input, clip-curation, and MonoDepth descriptions and clearer dataset positioning, while retaining the experimental evidence. These documentation gains are partly offset by the new 198-versus-199 Aria recording inconsistency and removal of the explicit baseline-code release commitment.
